DO NOT BUT THIS PRODUCT!! Not only was it a waste of $200, but it cost me several hundred dollars in spoiled food when it died within EIGHTEEN MONTHS of purchase. I had always assumed that Igloo had a good reputation for coolers, etc., but when I came back and looked at the reviews, I found that many others had the same problem. Well, Igloo denied any responsibility, and since their one-year warranty didn't cover it, I was out the cost of the freezer ($200) plus the food (somewhere between $350 & $450).  It seems that the light stays on, even though the cheap compressor they put in this thing gives out, so you don't even know it's not working, until you open it up to find several hundred dollars worth of food spoiled in a five-cubic-foot-deep puddle. I will never buy anything from Igloo ever again, at least not anything with a motor. Shame on them for such awful customer service, too. Igloo has proven that they do not care about their customers. I hope the $200 they got from me was worth it, for it is the last time I will buy one of their faulty products. So disappointed to see a once-reliable company refuse to acknowledge their flawed freezer (they wanted me to ship it back at my own cost and CHARGE ME TO FIX IT!) I will be telling all family and friends to avoid their products from now on.

First of all I did not buy one of these from Amazon but obtained one from someone who did. Theirs failed after 2 years, they tried to fix it and failed, and then gave it to me.. Reading these reviews I am seeing many of the same complaints.

After troubleshooting I found the Motor Starting Relay bad. Part number is QP2-4.7. You can buy them cheaply from Amazon. Or you can remove the Motor Starting Relay, Start Capacitor, and Motor Overload Switch and replace them with a Supco 3 n 1 Hard Start Kit for $12 and this will have a lot more reliability.

They are inexpensive and nice freezers however if you buy one you need to also buy a spare motor starting relay or a Supco 3 n 1 (RCO810) because this relay will fail in a year or two. I've seen it a lot of times and I'm reading about it here.

Anyone can change the relay in just a few minutes. It isn't hard. But mark my words. If you buy this freezer (also branded under IGLOO, CURTIS, THOMPSON, etc.) you need to also buy the starting relay for a spare.
